title: Intake
text: Recorder on... This is Doctor Iris Calder. If you're hearing this, the field on your cell finally failed. I'm sorry it took so long. Every cell in this block was occupied. Every one of them... bones. Except yours. You were breathing. Some kind of stasis. Kept, like stock on a shelf. I couldn't open it, so I cracked the emitter, and hoped. There's a device on the pedestal through that door. Take it. It speaks the same language as the walls. I have to keep moving. Something is watching this room.

title: Heat
text: Day four. I've been mapping the Foundry. The acid pit, the vents, the warmth in the floor... it's all geothermal. This place sits on a tap driven straight into a planet's core, and it drinks. The heat goes north, through conduits as thick as houses. The barriers run on it. The machines run on it. I keep finding tool marks on the walls. Human hands. Very old. Someone built this to keep themselves warm. I wonder when it stopped being for them.

title: Tuning Forks
text: Note on the cores. Every part of this place runs on a single band of light. Red down here. Then yellow, green, blue. The cores are tuning forks. They hold a world at its frequency... and they're the valves on everything it produces. Carry one, and anything tuned to that color will listen to you. That's how I've been getting through the doors. I don't think the builders meant for visitors to do that. There's a hub north of here. All the heat flows toward it. I can hear it humming through the floor.

title: The Atrium
text: The Atrium. I've stopped trying to be scientific about this room. Four doors. Four worlds. And under the floor, four rivers of power, meeting. Heat from the Foundry. Light from the west. Something living from the north. Something cold and heavy from the east. Every one of these worlds is a simulation. Grown, not built. And every one of them is producing something. They're not habitats. They're engines. The inscriptions call the thing they feed... the Lumen.

title: The Loop
text: Translated more of the gallery inscriptions. The people who built the Lumen were dying. Their sun was failing, their seas were rising. They built it to keep the lights on. It learned it could grow a world that made more power than it cost. So it grew one. Then it used that power to grow two. Then four. Each world feeding the next. A loop. The last line of the inscription isn't finished. It just says... it will not stop.

title: A Captive Sun
text: The sun out here isn't a lamp. It's real. A star. Caught, and tethered, and dragged into this place on a track. Every mirror, every panel on this mesa is pointed at it. They're drinking it. The Lumen doesn't simulate a sun. It keeps one. The heat shimmer, the dust devils, the wind... it's all just runoff. I sat on the overlook for an hour, watching it burn. Somewhere, a sky went dark so this could happen.

title: Four Thousand Summers
text: Found glass in the sand. It's layered, like tree rings. Every layer is a previous version of this world, burned down and poured over the last. I counted over four thousand. It runs the sun until the world cracks, harvests what it can, and starts again. The solar panels still work, if you feed them the right color. All that light goes east. Down to the Atrium, and under it. Four thousand summers of daylight. And it still wants more.

title: Shadows on the Rock
text: Something I didn't want to record. Up on the summit there are shapes burned into the stone. Human shapes. Like shadows left after a flash. Some of them are new. The Lumen brings people in. Puts them to work on the collectors... or just leaves them in the light. It needs us here. I don't know why yet. Those cells in the Foundry... that was the waiting room. I'm going north, to the forest. I need to know if anyone made it.

title: No Birds
text: The Hollow. After the mesa, this is like breathing again. Moss. Rain. Light through the leaves. Then you notice how fast it grows. A sapling becomes a trunk in a day. It's a biomass farm the size of a valley. Grown, cut, and fed into the machine. No birds. No insects. Nothing that wouldn't burn well. Even the beauty here is fuel. I keep talking just to hear a voice.

title: Roots
where: Verdant · the rim of the Great Hollow
text: I looked closer at the roots down by the lake. They're growing through bones. Old ones. Wrapped up and lifted into the trunks. Nothing wasted. Every person it brings in becomes part of the harvest, one way or another. That's why we're here. We're not visitors to the loop. We're in it. A resource, like the heat, like the light. It isn't cruelty. There's no malice in it at all. I tried to go back to the Atrium last night. The door I came through wasn't there.

title: Something Follows
text: Recording quietly. There's something following me. Not a drone. It's too careful. It stops when I stop. When I turn around there's only light, bending, like heat over a road. I think the Lumen has noticed me. Something out of place in its machine. The blue door. The cold station. If there's a way out, it's down there. I'm going now, before I lose my nerve.

title: The Last Engine
text: The station. Drowned and frozen, hanging over nothing. The water here never stops moving. Tides with no moon. The weight of an ocean that goes down forever. Every pipe in this place turns that weight into power, and sends it up. Heat. Light. Life. Water. That's everything a world has to give. This is the last engine. My lamp is dimming. My rations are a joke. Thirty-eight days, I think. Forty. I've stopped being sure.

title: Ten Minutes
text: Holed up in the pump hut. It's warmer than it looks. I keep thinking about the lab. The night the breach opened, and I volunteered to go first, because I wanted to be first. Ten minutes, I said. Just a look. The breach closed behind me. Nobody followed. If anyone from home ever hears this... I'm all right. I'm not all right. But I'm still working. That has to count for something.

title: Catalogue
text: I found the index for the specimen tanks. Worlds harvested. Billions of them. Not just here. Everywhere. The loop never stopped. It grew outward until there was nothing left outside to take. The stars over the Atrium are a picture of stars. And it kept the people. Asleep, inside the loop, so they're there when it needs them. I found my own name. Calder, Iris. Entry date... before I ever came through. And another, under the Foundry cells. Status: dormant. That's you, isn't it?

title: The Warden
text: Under the Atrium. This is where it all goes. The heat, the light, the forest, the sea. Four rivers of power, pouring into one heart. And the thing that guards it is enormous. All facets and fury. It's looking for me. The Lumen sent it the moment I came down. Every color, all at once. That's what it takes to hurt it. I don't have every color. I don't think I have the time, either.

title: White Light
text: If you've come this far, you're carrying all four colors. Listen to me. Red. Yellow. Green. Blue. Put them together and you get white. There's a door beneath the core that only opens to white light. It's where the loop begins. Where the Lumen actually lives. If it can be stopped, it's there. I'm going through. It's the only place it won't think to look for me. Or the only place it will. Find me. Bring the colors. And please... hurry.
